newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices fall on higher arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices fall on higher arrivals.

text.p: Indian cotton prices suffered a setback at improved levels on Tuesday, dealers said.

Mill demand was sluggish while higher prices attracted fresh offerings by state-owned agencies. "Cotton was up on Monday following lower arrivals due to cloudy weather and unseasonal rains in the Punjab region but arrivals again picked up today," one dealer said.
In spot deals Punjab saw-ginned fell by 5/10 rupees to 1,390/1,615 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi fell by 10/15 rupees to 790/825 rupees per maund.

Gujarat cotton however remained quiet amid limited activity. Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) was steady at 11,200/11,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) was steady at 16,500/18,000 rupees per candy.
